rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Titus left Caesarea, selected six hundred of his best soldiers at Jaffa, and approached Jerusalem to assess its defenses and seek peace.
rows.anchor: فسار منها حتى انتهى إلى يالو فأخذ من نقاوة عكسره ستمائة رجل

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Jerusalem’s gates were shut amid continuous factional fighting, so Titus found no one to negotiate with and turned back.
rows.anchor: وجد الأبواب مغلقة , وليس يخرج من المدينة ولا يدخل إليها أحد لما بين الخوارج من الحروب المتصلة

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Faction members ambushed Titus on his return; he barely escaped, learned the Jews’ courage and hostility, and prepared for the coming siege.
rows.anchor: أحاطوا به وحالوا بينه وبين أصحابه , فقاتلهم قتالا شديدا حتى خلص بعد أن أشرف على الهلاك

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: A brilliant star illuminated Jerusalem for seven nights during Passover; common people rejoiced, while scholars feared the omen.
rows.anchor: شبه كوكب كبير له نور قوي وضوء شديد كان القدس يضيء منه البلد كله طول الليل

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: At the festival, a cow brought for sacrifice gave birth to a lamb, which people found ominous.
rows.anchor: أحضروا في هذا العيد بقرة ليقربوها , فولدت خروفا فاستنكر الناس ذلك

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Jerusalem’s heavy eastern gate repeatedly stood open each day without anyone opening it; ordinary people celebrated, but scholars grieved.
rows.anchor: باب القدس الشرقي كان عظيما ثقيلا لا يعالجه إلا جماعة , فلما كان في تلك الأيام كانوا يجدونه كل يوم مفتوحا

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: A radiant human face appeared in the air above the Holy of Holies.
rows.anchor: ظهر على بيت قداس الأقداس في الهواء صورة وجه الإنسان شديد الحسن عظيم البهاء والنور

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Fiery riders appeared flying near the ground above Jerusalem and the whole land of the Jews.
rows.anchor: ظهر أيضا في الجو صور ركبان من نار يطيرون في الهواء قريبا من الأرض على بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: At Pentecost, priests heard many unseen people walking through the temple and then a great voice announcing that they should leave the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: سمع الكهنة في ليلة عيد العنصرة في القدس حس جماعة كثيرة يذهبون ويجيئون في الهيكل

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Four years before the siege, a man wandered Jerusalem crying that voices of doom came from every direction against the city, temple, fortress, cavalry, and people.
rows.anchor: ظهر قبل هذا بأربع سنين في المدينة رجل يمشي كالمجنون ويصيح بأعلى صوت يقول : صوت من المشرق

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: Residents dismissed the prophet as mad and rebuked him; he continued until the siege began, when a stone struck and killed him as he spoke.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل على ذلك إلى أن أحاط العدو بالمدينة , فابتدأ في بعض الأيام يتكلم على عادته , فأتاه حجر في رأسه فمات

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: An old stone said a great king would rule Israel and the wider earth once the temple became square; some identified him as Israel’s king, but priests and sages said he meant Rome.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم : هو ملك بني إسرائيل , وقال الحكماء والكهنة : بل الروم

rows.speaker: مؤرخهم
rows.claim: A second stone foretold Jerusalem’s destruction when its construction became square; dismantling Antonia and closing the wall made the temple square, while factional bloodshed, fire, and famine were the greatest warnings.
rows.anchor: إذا كمل بنيان القدس وصار مربعا فإنه عند ذلك يخرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus refused to flee, chose death over retreat, and kept fighting until he escaped after the Jews had overcome him three times.
rows.anchor: فاختار الموت على الهزيمة ولم يزل يقاتلهم حتى تخلص بعد أن استظهر عليه اليهود ثلاث دفعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterward the Jewish factions resumed their rivalry; John sought leadership, while Simon and Eleazar rejected his ambition.
rows.anchor: لأن يوحانان كان يريد الرئاسة , وكان شمعون والعازار يأبيان ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Passover John’s followers entered Jerusalem with weapons concealed beneath their clothes and killed many priests and residents, showing no mercy to young or old.
rows.anchor: فنزعوا ما ظهر من ثيابهم فإذا تحتها السلاح , وأخذوا على الناس الأبوابن فقتلوا خلقا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simon and Eleazar killed John’s followers who were outside the city, and the fighting between the factions continued.
rows.anchor: فقتل العازار وشمعون من كان خارج القدس من جماعة يوحانان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Jews offered Titus the gates in return for protection from the rebels, but he distrusted their treachery.
rows.anchor: نفتح لك الباب على أن تؤمننا وتريحنا من هؤلاء الخوارج , فلم يثق بهم لهم من شرهم وغدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city divided over admitting Rome; a group of Romans advanced, the rebels pelted them, and Jews then routed and pursued the Romans to their camp.
rows.anchor: لأن بعضهم كان يريد أن يفتح لطيطوس وبعضهم يمنع

rows.speaker: طيطوس
rows.claim: Titus rebuked his soldiers for disobeying his order to stay back, saying a Roman king had once killed his son for going to battle without permission.
rows.anchor: وقد علمتم أن بعض ملوكنا قتل ابنه لأنه مضى إلى الحرب بغير أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus ordered the area cleared, wells filled, walls prepared for assault, and surrounding orchards cut down; the Jews suspended infighting only when Romans threatened them.
rows.anchor: ويسدوا الآبار ليسهل عليهم القتال ويهدم السور , ففعلوا ذلك وقطعوا كل ما حول المدينة من الشجر والنبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rival forces included John’s 8,400 men, Simon’s 10,000 Jews and 5,000 Edomites, and priests and residents with Eleazar; they allied against Rome but fought each other when safe.
rows.anchor: وكان مع شمعون عشرة آلاف من اليهود وخمسة آلاف من أدوم - أي النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus brought battering equipment and wooden siege towers; after his peace envoy was killed, the factions united, burned the machinery, and then resumed their quarrels.
rows.anchor: وأرسل إليهم رجلا من أصحابه يدعوهم إلى المسالمة فرماه بعض من على السور فقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ram broke a large section of the first wall, but the Jews withdrew behind the second; renewed fighting left both sides committed, and Titus personally encouraged his soldiers with rewards.
rows.anchor: دفع الكبش علىالسور فهدم منه قطعة كبيرة , فهرب من كان وراءه إلى السور الثاني

rows.speaker: طيطوس
rows.claim: When Titus approached John’s lower wall, Castor pretended to negotiate to buy time, then tried to kill him with a thrown stone; Titus renewed the assault, and Castor killed himself.
rows.anchor: فألقى عليه صخرة فأخطأته وقتلت رجلا كان معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four days of fighting and new allied troops forced the Jews into the third fortress; Titus then suspended combat for five days and again offered peace before attacking the last wall.
rows.anchor: واتصلت الحرب بين الفريقين أربعة أيام , وورد على طيطوس في اليوم الرابع عسكر كبير من أمم مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus sent Joseph ben Gorion to offer safety and treaties, warning the leaders that two walls had fallen and the city and temple would be destroyed if they kept resisting.
rows.anchor: وأمر يوسف بن كريون أن يقرب منهم ويبلغ معهم الغاية في القول ويستدعيهم إلى المسالمة

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph argued that the Jews’ towns, troops, resources, and defenses were depleted, while Rome grew stronger; their sins, bloodshed, and desecration meant God had empowered Rome and would not aid them.
rows.anchor: فيجب أن علموا أنه هو الذي سلط عليكم هذه الأمة لسوء أفعالكم وكثرة ذنوبكم

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph says Israel had long obeyed Rome without considering submission a disgrace, and he urges renewed obedience to avoid death, loss of goods, and Jerusalem’s ruin.
rows.anchor: ثم أطاعوا بعد ذلك ملوك الروم إلى هذه الغاية , ولم يروا أن عليهم نقصا في طاعتهم

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: God gives each nation dominion for a time and then transfers it; Rome’s victories over stronger peoples showed that God now intended Rome to rule and Israel to submit.
rows.anchor: أن الله عز وجل قد جعل لكل أمة دولة وسلطانا سلطها فيه

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph says obeying a stronger power is neither shameful nor unusual; since Rome offered peace and security, surrender would preserve the survivors, Jerusalem, and the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فليس ينقصكم طاعة الروم , ولا الروم بأول من أطعتموهم وقد تقدمت طاعتكم لهم منذ سنين

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph says the rebels’ stated defense of the sanctuary and nation is hollow: their sins defiled the sacred place, and their own killings harmed Israel as much as any enemy could.
rows.anchor: فأنتم قد ابتذلتموه بالمعاصي نجستموه بما سفكتم فيه من الدماء الكثير ظلما

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph argues Israel’s past victories came through obedience, prayer, and God’s aid, not merely armies; when they disobeyed, God handed them over despite their weapons and numbers.
rows.anchor: فلما عصوه سلط عليهم الأعداء ومكنهم منهم حتى قهروهم وأذلوهم

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: As an example, God afflicted Pharaoh after he took Abraham’s wife, then returned her unharmed and honored Abraham, showing that deliverance came through piety and prayer rather than warfare.
rows.anchor: اعتبروا بأبيكم إبراهيم عليه السلام لما أخذ فرعون امرأته أمل يضرب الله فرعون وأهله بالبلاء العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After earlier mercy, Titus refused John and Simon’s late request for safety; their followers killed Roman commanders, Titus retaliated, and the two leaders eventually emerged from hiding and were executed.
rows.anchor: فانحدرا ليلا إلى القدس بأصحابهما فتلوا قائدين من الروم فأمر طيطوس بقتل من بقي في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus took captives and spoils toward Rome, while Eleazar left before the city fell, fortified a refuge, and led his followers to kill their families and fight to death rather than be captured.
rows.anchor: فلما عاين الهلكة دعا أصحابه إلى قتل قتل من خلفهم من العيال والاستقتال ليموتوا أعزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the former deliverance, God raises hope of renewed mercy and repentance; if Israel returns to sin again, God will return to punishing them in this world.
rows.anchor: { عسى ربكم } أي الذي عودكم بإحسانه { أن يرحمكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording is knowingly framed as a warning despite God’s knowledge that Israel repeatedly returned to wrongdoing, distinguishing divine speech from ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: وقد عادوا غير مرة بما أشار إليه الكلام , وإن كان في سياق الشرط , ليظهر الفرق بين كلام العالم ويغره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted Torah promises that dispersed Israel can repent, return wholeheartedly to God, be gathered from every nation, restored to its land, multiplied, and given circumcised hearts.
rows.anchor: فيجمعك من جميع الشعوب التي فرقك فيها , وإن كان المبددون يا آل إسرائيل في أقطار الأرض يجمعك الله ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s examples include God helping Isaac when Abimelech took his wife, freeing Israel from Pharaoh through divine aid, and granting victory over Amalek through Moses’ prayer.
rows.anchor: إسحاق عليه السلام لما أخذ أبيمالخ ملك فلسطين امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua did not take Jericho through ordinary battle; its walls fell through a remarkable sign.
rows.anchor: فهل فتح يريحا بالحرب أو بالآية العجيبة في سقوط الحصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Achan’s forbidden taking of Jericho’s spoils brought Israel defeat by the smaller force at Ai until Joshua prayed and God restored victory.
rows.anchor: حتى غلبهم أهل مدينة عاي وهم قليل , فلم يقدر بنو إسرائيل مع كثرتهم على مقاومتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gideon defeated the numerous Midianite and Amalekite forces only through God’s assistance.
rows.anchor: وجدعون لما غلب عسكر مدين وعماليق مع كثرتهم هل غلبهم إلا بمعونة الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talut was supported while obedient but abandoned to his enemies after disobedience; Amaziah likewise lost divine aid after setting idols in the temple.
rows.anchor: طالوت - الملك لما كان طائعا لله تعالى كان الله ينصره , فلما عصاه أسلمه الله إلى أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Amaziah defeated Edom and installed its idols in Jerusalem’s temple, God withdrew support, and Joash of Israel defeated him badly.
rows.anchor: فلما أخذ اصنامهم ونصبها في بيت المقدس سخط الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sennacherib’s great army was destroyed without battle through Hezekiah’s and the prophets’ prayers.
rows.anchor: هلاك عسكر سنحاريب ملك الموصل العسكر العظيم بغير حرب ولا قتال بل بصلاة حزقيا الملك والأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zedekiah resisted the Chaldeans and ignored the prophets while trusting his army, bringing destruction on himself and his people.
rows.anchor: هل انتفع بذلك ؟ وهل كانت عاقبته وعاقبة الأمة إلا إلى الهلاك

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph says Vespasian treated him kindly and forgave him despite his resistance; he argues this proves Rome may spare those who submit, whereas the rebels would have killed him for dissent.
rows.anchor: ثم حصلت مع الروم فما أساؤوا إلي بل أحسنوا وأجملوا وعفو عني وأنا معهم إلى هذه الغاية

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph takes the spring of Siloam swelling from near-dryness to a river as a sign that God would help Rome; he urges surrender to preserve Jerusalem, whose survival sustains Israel’s honor.
rows.anchor: فإنها قد كانت قريبة من الجفاف قبل أن ينزل بكم هذه العساكر , فلما نزلوا غزرت فصارت كالنهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus released captives and allowed people to leave, but rebels guarded the gates and killed anyone trying to escape as the siege and famine intensified.
rows.anchor: وأطلق لهم أن يمضوا حيث شاؤوا فمال أكثر أهل المدينة إلى طاعة طيطوس , فمنعهم الخوارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebels searched homes, seized food, and killed those who resisted; would-be foragers were killed by rebels inside or Romans outside, while Titus pitied the starving residents.
rows.anchor: فكان الناس يموتون في المدينة بالجوع , ومن أراد الخروج إلى ظاهر المدينة ليأخذ شيئا من نبات الأرض قتله الخوارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus attacked the third wall from four sides, but Jewish fighters burned the siege rams and equipment and routed the Romans before Titus rallied them.
rows.anchor: فخرج إليهم الخوارج فقاتلوهم قتالا شديدا , وقتلوا من الروم خلقا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus then blockaded Jerusalem to starve it; residents could not grind or cook without theft or detection, the dead filled the streets, and bodies were thrown into the eastern valley.
rows.anchor: فضبطوا جميع طرق المدينة , فضاق الأمر بهم جدا واشتد الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy woman with one young son lost her food to the rebels; as he suffered from hunger and both seemed doomed, she resolved to kill and eat him.
rows.anchor: فلما قويت المجاعة , ونهب الخوارج جميع ما عندها , اشتد بها الأمر وكان ابنها تضور من الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman says she will kill and eat her son so he will not be left unburied or eaten by animals, turning her act into a lasting indictment of the rebels who caused the famine.
rows.anchor: وأنا وأنت هالكان , وإن مت يا بني لم يدفنك أحد وكنت كغيرك ممن أكلته الكلاب وطيور السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She killed, roasted, and ate her child, then offered the remaining body to the rebels and challenged their courage and responsibility for the calamity.
rows.anchor: قتلته بيدي لإفراط الجوع وأكلت من لحمه , وهذا بقية جسمه عزلتها لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebels recoiled and fled; the incident spread, residents recognized the announced divine warning, and the rebels let many people leave.
rows.anchor: وتحققوا صحة الوعيد الذي سبق من الله , وانكسر الخوارج لذلك واستعظموه وأطلقوا للناس الخروج

rows.speaker: طيطوس
rows.claim: Titus prayed that God not hold him responsible for the woman’s suffering, affirming he had not come to harm Jerusalem’s people and asking God to punish the rebels and grant him victory.
rows.anchor: أنت تعلم أني لم أجئ إلى هذه المدينة لأسيء إلى أهلها ولقد ساءني أمر هذه المرأة فلا تؤاخذني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many starving escapees died when they suddenly ate; Joseph advised gradually giving them milk and thin soup before food, which saved some.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن يسقوا اللبن والحساء الرقيق أياما حتى تلين أمعاؤهم , ثم الطعام بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Romans broke the third wall, Jews built a new wall overnight and repelled them; the Romans despaired of taking the city and considered leaving.
rows.anchor: إذا سور جديد بإزاء الهدم قد بناه اليهود تلك الليلة وهم قيام عليه

rows.speaker: طيطوس
rows.claim: Titus rallied his soldiers by arguing that abandoning the nearly completed siege would waste their effort and invite contempt, while Jewish endurance made Roman perseverance more necessary.
rows.anchor: فأن انصرفتم كنتم قد ضيعتم تعبكم وأنتم علىأنفسكم أهنتموها عند كل من يسمع خبركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Romans entered through a breach at night and fought the exhausted Jews in the outer court; after repelling them, the Jews incorporated Antonia’s gap into the wall, making Jerusalem square and recalling the stone’s doom prophecy.
rows.anchor: فصار مربعا , فكان ذلك تصديق ما رأوه قبل ذلك مكتوبا على الحجر القديم المقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: طيطوس
rows.claim: At Pentecost Titus urged peace by contrasting Jeconiah’s surrender to Nebuchadnezzar, which saved his people, with Zedekiah’s resistance to prophetic advice, which destroyed city and nation.
rows.anchor: فسبيلكم أن تعبروا بهما وتهتدوا بأصوبهما فعلا وأحمدهما عاقبة

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Joseph says Daniel foretold the end of sacrifices and priesthood, yet the Jews still refuse humility and submission to the power God has imposed.
rows.anchor: تقرؤون كتاب دانيال النبي عليه السلام وتعلمون ما ذكره من بطلان القرابين وعدم الكاهن المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some priests and leaders escaped to Rome and received safe conduct, but rebels barred others; Roman forces entered the sanctuary to rescue them and were driven into the Holy of Holies, where Jews killed them.
rows.anchor: فبادر الروم ليخلصوهم فهجموا إلى القدس فقاتلوهم قتالا شديدا فانهزم الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Romans were killed in the sanctuary, Titus selected thirty thousand soldiers and planned a night attack, though his companions initially stopped him from entering personally.
rows.anchor: فاختار طيطوس من عسكره ثلاثين ألفا وأمرهم أن يدخلوا إلى صحن القدس لمحاربتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews fought at the sanctuary gates for seven days, killing many Romans and driving them away; Titus then halted combat so hunger would weaken the defenders.
rows.anchor: وأقاموا على مقاتلة الروم سبعة أيام , فقتلوا منهم جماعة كثرة وأبعدوهم عن القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hidden Jew set fire to the wooden upper floor of Solomon’s palace, trapping Roman soldiers behind a blocked entrance; many prominent Romans died, and the frightened survivors abandoned the city.
rows.anchor: فخرج اليهودي الذي كان قد اختفى , فاختلط بهم وأطلق النار في تلك المواضع , فاضطرمت النار في جميع جوانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Simon’s followers sought protection, he killed their leaders, while the rest fled to Titus and were spared.
rows.anchor: فقتل شمعون رؤساءهم وهرب الباقون إلى طيطوس فآمنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titus refused John and Simon’s late request for safety, reminding them that he had offered it earlier and that they were now in his power.
rows.anchor: فقال : قد كنت طلبت إليكما ذلك قبل , فأما الآن فأنتما في قبضتي وليس لي عذر عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their night raid killed two Roman commanders, Titus ordered the remaining Jews he had previously spared to be killed.
rows.anchor: فقتلوا قائدين من الروم فأمر طيطوس بقتل من بقي في المدينة من اليهود ممن كان قدر رحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Priests who could no longer defend the temple threw themselves into the fire; residents burned the city’s palaces and homes, and the temple burned on the same tenth of Av as the first temple.
rows.anchor: وكان حريق القدس في اليوم العاشر من الشهر الخامس وهو آب , وذلك نظير اليوم الذي أحرق فيه الكسدانيون البيت الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophet promised the temple would be rebuilt by God rather than human builders and urged continued resistance; the Romans defeated his followers and killed many Jews previously spared.
rows.anchor: بل بقدرة الله تعالى , فداموا على ما أنتم عليه من محارب الروم والامتناع من طاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John and Simon fled to hide at Mount Zion; after Titus took the city and demolished the wall, they emerged from hunger and were killed, and Titus departed with captives and spoils.
rows.anchor: خرجا إلى طيطوس فقتلهما , ثم رحل متوجها إلى روميه ومعه السبي والغنائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eleazar fortified a refuge after leaving Jerusalem; when Titus’s commander besieged him, Eleazar persuaded his companions to kill their families and fight to the death, and all were killed.
rows.anchor: دعا أصحابه إلى قتل من خلفهم من العيال والاستقتال ليموتوا أعزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the devastation, God offers the possibility of mercy through repentance, since He has previously shown Israel kindness and can restore them.
rows.anchor: { عسى ربكم } أي الذي عودكم بإحسانه { أن يرحمكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel returns to disobedience, God will again punish them in this world; although phrased conditionally, the repeated returns are already known to God, distinguishing divine speech from ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: { وإن عدتم } أي بما نعلم من دبركم إلى المعصية مرة ثالثة فما فوقها { عدنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Torah passage promises that repentant dispersed Israel will be gathered from the nations, returned to ancestral land, multiplied, and given circumcised hearts and blessing.
rows.anchor: ويردك إلى الأرض التي ورثها أبوكم وترثون , وينعم عليكم وتكثرون أفضل من آبائكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The author reads Gehenna as a confining prison, while al-Hasan says al-hasīr is something spread out as bedding; calling the condemned disbelievers signals that the label itself grounds the judgment and that some Israelites believe while others disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أن الحصير هو الذي يفرش ويبسط , فالمعنى أنه يجعلها مهادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah guided Israel and its promises and warnings were fulfilled in their history: obedience brought honor, while disobedience repeatedly brought enemy killing, captivity, plunder, and ruined lands; the Qur’an surpasses it in every noble quality.
rows.anchor: لاح أن القرآن يزيد عليه في كل معنى حسن وأمر شريف فيما أتى به من الوعود الصادقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s excellence parallels Muhammad’s journey to Jerusalem exceeding Moses’ journey there, where Moses received the scripture.
rows.anchor: بنسبة ما زاد المسير المحمدي إلى بيت المقدس - الذي أراه فيه من آياته - على المسير الموسوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an gathers every truth and distinguishes what is confused; omitting the described noun before allati gives grandeur and wonder through the phrase’s deliberate ambiguity.
rows.anchor: الجامع لكل حق والفارق بين كل ملتبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most upright way exceeds paths in earlier scriptures through clearer expression, promises for all people in both worlds, analogies, removal of doubts, clear proofs, and rulings that are sometimes easier and otherwise superior.
rows.anchor: أما في الصورة فباعتبار ما علا من البيان , وأما في الوعود فباعتبار العموم لجميع الخلق في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are those whose faith is renewed and demonstrated by ongoing righteous deeds; their great reward indicates this community’s religious stability and continuing prominence, unlike the Israelites’ foretold corruption.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى صلاح هذه الأمة وثباتهم على دينهم وأنه لا يزال أمرهم ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an also promises punishment for those who reject the afterlife; their lack of faith means they do not perform righteous deeds truly, or their deeds lack a foundation in faith.
rows.anchor: بالآخرة } حقيقة أو مجازا , المسبب عنه أنهم لا يعلمون الصالحات حقيقة لعدم مباشرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase prepared for them is ironic, as if their painful punishment were a desirable provision, and it emphasizes God’s certain prior preparation of it.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالعتاد تهكما بهم , فقال تعالى : { أعتدنا } أي أحضرنا وهيأنا ما هو في غاية الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may invoke harm against himself or loved ones in anger while intending the good; this reveals foolishness, weak judgment, and forgetfulness of what would benefit him.
rows.anchor: حذف واوه - الذي هو لام الفعل - خطأ في جميع المصاحف ولا موجب لحذفه لفظا في العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written omission of the wāw in yadʿu is not required in pronunciation; the author reads it as signaling foolish desire for harm and an action tending toward ruin until God intervenes, referring to stopping rules in al-Qamar.
rows.anchor: مشير إلى أنه يدعو بالشر لسفهه وقلة عقله , وهو لا يريد علو الشر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are innately hasty and rush toward whatever occurs to them without considering its proper moment; they may seek punishment mockingly for themselves or vindictively for others.
rows.anchor: يتسرع إلى طلب كل ما يقع في قلبه ويخطر بباله من غير أن يتأنى فيه تأني المتبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjala means seeking something before its proper time, whereas surʿa means acting at the earliest time that is proper for it.
rows.anchor: والعجلة : طلب الشيء في غير وقته الذي لا يجوز تقديمه عليه , وأما السرعة فهي عمله في أول وقته
